On this page

If you are a software developer looking to build an integration with SavvyCal Meetings, you're in the right place! We offer several ways to integrate with our product, including a REST API, webhooks, and a JavaScript embed library.

## REST API[​](#rest-api "Direct link to REST API")
The SavvyCal API adheres to [REST](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_State_Transfer) conventions. Our API communicates in JSON format and uses [OAuth access tokens](/authentication) to authenticate requests. We take an additive approach; new fields may be added to existing payload types as we expand the API.

The server-side REST API is available at:

```
https://api.savvycal.com/
```

[**Start exploring endpoints →**](/category/rest-api)

## JavaScript Embed[​](#javascript-embed "Direct link to JavaScript Embed")
Our JavaScript library allows you to embed your scheduling links on your website (both inline and as a popover). [Learn more about embedding →](https://docs.savvycal.com/article/6-embedding-links-on-your-website)

## Webhooks[​](#webhooks "Direct link to Webhooks")
Webhooks allow you to listen for changes in a SavvyCal account and get notified via HTTP POST requests. [Learn more about webhooks →](/webhooks)

title: Custom domains - Meetings Help
content:
# Custom domains
SavvyCal links, profile pages, and meeting polls are hosted on [savvycal.com](http://savvycal.com) by default. If you're looking for a more white-labeled feel, the custom domains feature in SavvyCal gives you the ability to host your scheduling links, profiles, and polls on your own custom domain (e.g., `booking.example.com/noah/chat` ).

This feature is available on the SavvyCal Premium plan.

## Adding a custom domain
To add a custom domain to your SavvyCal account, head to your [Settings](https://savvycal.com/me/settings), scroll down to "Custom Domains, " and click *Add a custom domain*.

You'll want to point a **subdomain** (e.g. *meet*.example.com) to SavvyCal, not your bare domain (e.g. *example.com*, since this is where your actual website is hosted).

![](//d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/5efe16a12c7d3a10cba9eca4/images/66fc39d2e6b2356def90a364/file-D0NtArj5MV.png)

## Configuring your DNS settings
The precise steps for doing this vary depending on where your domain is registered and where your DNS is hosted (sometimes they are two different places). But essentially, you'll need to add a CNAME record to your DNS pointing to SavvyCal.

The **Record Name** should be the subdomain where you want to serve your links. For example, if you want to serve them at `meet.example.com`, then you'd create a CNAME for the `meet` subdomain pointing to `custom.savvycal.com` in your DNS settings.

| Type | Record Name | Record Value | TTL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CNAME | `meet` or `meet.` | `custom.savvycal.com` | Auto |

You may need to include a trailing "." at the end of your subdomain when creating your CNAME record (e.g. **meet.** instead of **meet**).

Once we confirm your DNS settings are all in place, we'll activate the domain in your SavvyCal account so you can start using it!

## Assigning a custom domain to individuals and teams
Once your DNS settings are confirmed, you'll be able to assign the domain to individual users and teams that belong to your organization. To do this, click the toggle next to the person or team:

![](//d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/5efe16a12c7d3a10cba9eca4/images/66fc3baa44628317ef90485c/file-ks4aw9gmhs.png)

From there, you can either assign this scope to a **subdirectory** (e.g. *example.com/derrick*) or to the **root domain** (e.g. *example.com*).

Only one individual or team can be assigned to the root domain, so you will usually want to assign it to a team that represents your company, rather than a single person.

![](//d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/5efe16a12c7d3a10cba9eca4/images/66fc3c15dd5b956281ae59b5/file-Q7L8wSe3pa.png)

![](//d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/5efe16a12c7d3a10cba9eca4/images/66fc3d0ddd5b956281ae59b6/file-CJIHC954Ys.png)

That's it! Now, when you copy the URL for your scheduling links, we'll use your configured custom domain in the URL.

![](//d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/5efe16a12c7d3a10cba9eca4/images/66fc3d3a8af27b34842bf6b9/file-9f1mYOo6jn.png)

Your links will **continue to work with their original savvycal.com URL**, so you don't need to worry if you've already shared those URLs!

Still need help?
[Contact Us](#)

Last updated on January 1, 2025

title: Configuring link availability - Meetings Help
content:
# Configuring link availability
Buffers allow you to enforce rules around how closely new events can be scheduled next to existing events on your calendar. You can configure your [default settings here](https://savvycal.com/settings/links) (scroll down to "Buffers"), or on an individual link-basis (under the **Availability** section).

## Buffers
There are a number of different settings you can configure:

- **Buffer Before**: the minimum amount of time to keep open before a new event.
- **Buffer After**: the minimum amount of time to keep open after a new event.
- **Minimum Notice**: the minimum amount of lead time required before the start of a new event.
- **Start Time Increments**: how frequently we should generate time slots within a given range of time (every 15 minutes, every 30 minutes, or every hour).

Suppose you want to make sure you have 10 minutes of free time before a call to prepare, and 30 minutes of time reserved after a call (in case it runs a little bit over time). You can enforce these constraints like this:

![](//d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/5efe16a12c7d3a10cba9eca4/images/66d1306b65e01777a9334a58/file-JdjEaipWhV.png)

## Frequency Limits
If you'd like to ensure that a maximum number of events are booked through your link on a given day, week, or month, you can toggle on *Limit scheduling frequency* and define one or more limits.

![](//d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/5efe16a12c7d3a10cba9eca4/images/66d131cd6eb51e63b8f9fc07/file-XJiSYenRj5.png)

### Wait, are my buffers appearing backward?
Buffer settings be a bit confusing! Here's an elaborate explanation.

Suppose you have a non-SavvyCal-initiated event on your calendar called "Busy Event" and you've configured your link to have 10 minutes before and 30 minutes after buffers. Since this "Busy Event" doesn't have any buffers of its own, this is how it will be padded on your scheduling link:

![](//d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/5efe16a12c7d3a10cba9eca4/images/60900dba8996210f18bd99c3/file-0k7cTIH1Rx.png)

Initially, this looks backward: why is my 30-minute "after buffer" occurring *before* the event? The reason is because the buffers apply to the (hypothetical) new event that someone might schedule in those spots, so the 30-minute after buffer applies to the range of time before that already-existing event.

Still need help?
[Contact Us](#)

Last updated on January 1, 2025

title: Group scheduling mode - Meetings Help
content:
# Group scheduling mode
Group scheduling mode allows accepting more than one scheduler for each time slot on your scheduling links. This comes in handy if you are offering things like group coaching sessions, webinars, and office hours. In this guide, we'll walk you through how group scheduling works.

## Creating a group scheduling link
To get started, create a scheduling link by clicking the **New** menu in the sidebar and choosing *Scheduling Link*.

![](//d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/5efe16a12c7d3a10cba9eca4/images/662a7e837303ea4a739d3854/file-aqrOwgWmRN.png)

Then, click the **Link Type** section and change the Mode to Group.

![](//d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/5efe16a12c7d3a10cba9eca4/images/662a7ef7e66450147a8e5cc2/file-Tjzv3AOQHa.png)

You can then configure the maximum number of schedulers allowed to book the same time slot using the *Maximum group size* setting.

![](//d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/5efe16a12c7d3a10cba9eca4/images/662a7f245ae8353469c6adc5/file-dtbPuTKLYy.png)

Finally, click **Save** to save your changes. That's it!

We'll notify the link organizer anytime someone books a time on a new (or existing) time slot.

- If an event already exists and has not reached the maximum group size, we'll present that time slot as open and automatically add the person to the existing event.
- If the event has reached the maximum number of attendees, it will be shown as busy on your scheduling link.
- If all the schedulers on a group event cancel, we'll automatically cancel the underlying calendar event.

Still need help?
[Contact Us](#)
